lesson.title: Squares and cubes
points: The square of a number is the number multiplied by itself, so 7² = 7 × 7 = 49.
The cube of a number is the number multiplied by itself three times, so 4³ = 4 × 4 × 4 = 64.
A square root or cube root undoes squaring or cubing: √49 = 7 and ∛64 = 4.
To find a root, write the number as a product of primes and make groups: pairs for a square root, triples for a cube root.
lesson.story: A floor is covered with square tiles in 12 rows of 12 tiles each. The number of tiles is 12² = 144, and going back from 144 tiles to the 12 tiles along one side is taking the square root.

steps: Take one prime from each pair and multiply: 2 × 2 × 7 = 28.

lesson.title: Powers made easy
points: aᵐ × aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ and aᵐ ÷ aⁿ = aᵐ⁻ⁿ: with the same base, add powers when multiplying and subtract when dividing.
(aᵐ)ⁿ = aᵐⁿ: a power of a power means multiply the powers.
a⁰ = 1 for any non-zero a, and a⁻ⁿ = 1/aⁿ, so 2⁻³ = 1/8.
Very big or very small numbers are written in standard form as k × 10ⁿ with 1 ≤ k < 10.
lesson.story: A forwarded message is sent on to 2 new people, who each send it to 2 more, and so on. After 5 rounds, 2⁵ = 32 people get it, and going back one round divides by 2.

steps: Same base in the product, so add the powers: 2³ × 2⁵ = 2⁸.
Now divide by 2⁴: subtract the powers, 2⁸ ÷ 2⁴ = 2⁴.

lesson.title: Identities save time
points: To multiply expressions, multiply every term of one by every term of the other and then add the like terms.
(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² and (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b².
(a + b)(a − b) = a² − b².
(x + a)(x + b) = x² + (a + b)x + ab. These identities make big calculations like 102² quick.

lesson.title: Balancing equations
points: An equation is like a balanced scale: whatever you do to one side, do to the other side as well.
Moving a term to the other side (transposing) changes its sign: + becomes − and × becomes ÷.
Collect the x terms on one side and the numbers on the other, then divide by the coefficient of x.
Check your answer by putting it back into the equation: both sides must be equal.

lesson.title: Percent, profit and interest
points: Per cent means out of 100. 25% of 80 is 25/100 × 80 = 20.
Profit or loss is always found on the cost price: Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100. Discount is taken off the marked price.
Simple interest SI = P × R × T / 100, where the interest is the same every year.
In compound interest the interest of each year is added to the principal, so Amount = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ and CI = Amount − P.
lesson.story: During a Diwali sale a shirt marked ₹800 gets 10% off. The shopkeeper takes ₹80 off the marked price, and you pay ₹720.

lesson.title: Area, surface and volume
points: Area of a trapezium = ½ × (sum of the parallel sides) × (distance between them).
Cuboid: volume = l × b × h and total surface area = 2(lb + bh + hl). Cube: volume = a³ and surface area = 6a².
Cylinder: curved surface area = 2πrh, total surface area = 2πr(r + h) and volume = πr²h.
Area is in square units, volume is in cubic units, and 1 m³ = 1000 litres.

lesson.title: Data and chance
points: Mean = (sum of all values) ÷ (number of values). Mode is the value that occurs most often.
Median is the middle value after arranging the data in order. With an even number of values, it is the average of the two middle values.
In a pie chart, the angle for a part = (part ÷ whole) × 360°.
Probability = (number of favourable outcomes) ÷ (total equally likely outcomes). It is always between 0 and 1.

lesson.title: Four-sided shapes
points: The angles of a quadrilateral add up to 360°. Splitting it by a diagonal gives two triangles of 180° each.
For an n-sided polygon, the sum of interior angles is (n − 2) × 180°, and the exterior angles always add up to 360°.
In a parallelogram, opposite sides are equal and parallel, opposite angles are equal, and adjacent angles add up to 180°.
A rhombus has four equal sides and its diagonals cut each other at right angles. A rectangle has equal diagonals and four right angles.
lesson.story: A kite-maker cuts a diamond-shaped frame from two bamboo sticks that cross each other at right angles in the middle. The sticks are the diagonals of the frame.
